title: Code as the source of truth
summary: Projects now live locally, with code as the database for your video projects. Agents can work directly from the source code, your editing decisions can become reusable skills, and every change can be tracked with Git.
body_markdown:
Code is the new database.


Projects in the desktop app now live in local source files, replacing browser storage. You can open them in your preferred code editor, organize them alongside your other work, and manage them with your own tools. Your project becomes a codebase you and your agent can work on together.


## Your changes stay in context


Visual editing and code stay in sync. It works both ways: changes in the editor update the source code, and changes in code update the editor instantly on save. Think of it as an IDE for video, where you render code as video.


Adjust the spacing of a title or move an animation by a single frame. The source records those choices as precise values your agent can read, reuse, and compare across versions.


The project also saves your canvas zoom and position, giving your agent context about where you’re working alongside the changes you’ve made.


0:00 / 0:00


## Ready for your agent


Every project comes with source files, an asset library, and instructions that point your agent to the editing docs and examples included with the desktop app.


The app saves changes to the composition and asset library in the project folder. Imported media stays in its original location, linked through the asset library, while generated media is saved in the project’s assets folder.


If you prefer to keep media with the project, place it in the project folder before importing, or ask your agent to move it there and update the file references.


## Turn your edits into reusable skills


The work you put into one video can become a workflow for future projects. Your layout, typography, timing, and animation are recorded in code, giving your agent a precise starting point for a reusable skill. That skill can combine the code with instructions for adapting it to new content.


You can also ask your agent to create project templates or shared components from the same work. Reuse a title sequence across episodes, adapt a product video for another launch, or create versions in several languages. Each follows the design choices and production rules you’ve already established.


## Track changes with Git


Keep your project code in Git to compare edits, restore earlier versions, and explore alternatives on branches. Changes made in the editor and by your agent can be reviewed and committed together.


A shared repository can also support video production across a company. A design team can maintain the formats and production rules, while marketing, sales, and regional teams use them with their agents. Teams can review proposed changes before adopting them.


## Added


- Added` check` , so agents can find black frames, elements that never appear, and broken media before export
- Added drag and drop reordering of timeline layers
- Added ⌘↩ to wrap the selection in a scene
- Added ⌘⌥↩ to wrap the selection in a sequence
- Added ⌘⌥⇧↩ to unwrap a sequence
- Added ⌘⇧G to ungroup any group, sequence, or scene
- Added a projects folder picker and a Reveal in Finder button to the dashboard
- Added a confirmation before deleting a project
- Added a splash screen while the app loads


## Fixed


- Fixed generated media being lost after restarting the app
- Fixed volume animation ramping in the audio panel
- Fixed project folder paths with a trailing slash being rejected
- Fixed generated images and videos not keeping their aspect ratio when resized
- Fixed the aspect ratio picker using video settings for image prompts
- Fixed marquee selection picking elements hidden behind a scene
- Fixed the rename field losing focus after the context menu in the dashboard
- Fixed removing a linked asset touching the original file outside the project


## Improved


- Improved project covers, now saved as a file in the project folder
- Improved thumbnail and waveform loading with a cache folder
- Improved auto captions to match scene length and to re-transcribe on demand
- Improved` capture` to render frames the same way export does
- Improved export settings to update when the source changes
- Improved the source settings in the inspector with a fit menu and a color and opacity picker
- Improved unnamed clips to show a label based on their type
- Improved the soundboard layout on small windows
- Improved the minimum screen size message
